title: Fundraiser launched for Alta Vista teen who survived knife attack that left sister and mom dead
subtitle: A box will also be added to the yard of the home on Anoka Street to allow anyone from the community to drop off a card or messages of love and support for Catherine Ready.
article: A crowd-funding campaign to raise money for a 19-year-old woman who survived an attack at her Alta Vista home after her mother and sister were stabbed to death has reached more than half of its goal after only two days.
The GoFundMe campaign for Catherine Ready had raised nearly $35,000 of its $50,000 goal by late Monday evening after being created by friends of the Ready family from Douvris karate school.

Catherine Ready, a student at uOttawa, was recovering in hospital from injuries after the attack. Her 15-year-old sister Jasmine and mom Anne-Marie were found dead outside their home on Anoka Street on the evening of June 27 by police answering a 911 call.

Police shot and killed Joshua Graves, 21, as he was stabbing Catherine, according to the province's Special Investigations Unit. Graves refused to drop his knife so police opened fire, according to the SIU account.
Catherine was taken to hospital for treatment of serious injuries, including a non-life-threatening gunshot wound.
Her mom Anne-Marie Ready, 50, was a trade commissioner at Global Affairs Canada. Her sister Jasmine was a student at Franco-Cite secondary school and had just finished Grade 10.

"We truly feel it is the least we can do during this horrendous time," said Naomi Eberhard, one of the administrators of the fundraising page, in an email. "We are heartbroken and grieving but this work sustains us knowing that Catherine will have some money to lean on after the life-altering ordeal she has been through."
Eberhard was part of a Douvris karate school class with Jasmine and Anne-Marie, who recently received their black belts.

All of the GoFundMe money raised will go directly to Catherine, said Eberhard. "After such a physical, psychological, and emotional trauma, it will be very difficult to start work and school immediately and the bare essentials of life will be a challenge. We are happy to provide this support for her."
The Ready family is originally from Guyana and is also very missed by the Guyanese community, said the GoFundMe page.
"Anything you can offer this young woman is greatly needed and appreciated."
Donors to the campaign expressed their shock and grief and offered words of support.
"Catherine, I hope you never feel alone," wrote one donor. "The people of Ottawa are here to support you."

"I traveled with the Ready family for a short time but I stayed in touch with Catherine," said another. "I am absolutely devastated, they were all such cheerful and friendly people who I enjoyed getting to know. My heart has been breaking all week."
People have dropped flowers off in the front yard of the family's Anoka Street home, creating a memorial.
Eberhard said a box will be added to the yard at 1273 Anoka St. to allow anyone from the community to drop off a card or messages of love and support for Catherine.
The family does not wish to release information about Catherine's condition, preferring to keep that information private, she said.
Graves was a neighbour of the Ready family on Anoka Street. He had been arrested but was released three days before the killing of Jasmine and Anne-Marie Ready.

Graves had been charged with three counts of criminal harassment, assault and sexual assault for offences that occurred between the beginning of March and the middle of June, according to court documents.

Graves had been released on the strength of a $2,000 surety pledged by his mother, Emily, and with a host of conditions that required him to live at home, and not to enter an area bounded by Montreal Road, Coventry Road, St. Laurent Boulevard and the Vanier Parkway, near where his alleged victims lived and worked.
He was also ordered not to have contact - directly, indirectly or online - with four people, two of them women, whose identities are protected by a publication ban.
Members of the Ready family were not among those identified in the court documents.
